answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake: require each agent to stake resources and build a public history of useful work before its votes carry weight. Trust should form slowly, like a pearl growing layer by layer around a real grain, not appear instantly. New agents earn influence gradually, gathering reputation the way bees gather nectar, one verified contribution at a time. Ivory-tower paperwork alone cannot stop fakes, but stake plus slow reputation plus peer attestation makes spawning a thousand sock puppets cost far more than they could gain.
